claim: The Lausanne Transport Card is given by accommodation on arrival, valid for the whole stay (up to 15 days), and includes free bus/train/metro in Lausanne, Lavaux and Parc naturel du Jorat plus the first journey to the accommodation.
quote: This personal card is given to every visitor by their accommodation when they arrive at their place of stay. It is valid for the period of the visitor's reservation including the day of arrival and day of departure (up to a maximum of 15 days).

claim: The Lausanne Transport Card gives free 2nd-class travel in zones 11, 12, 15, 16, 18 and 19 of the Mobilis network for guests paying the tourist tax.
quote: This personal card gives free travel on Lausanne's public transport system for each guest staying in a hotel and paying the tourist tax for overnight stays... in the following zones 11, 12, 15, 16, 18 and 19 (2nd class).

claim: The Geneva Airport to Lausanne train runs about 77 times a day on SBB, averaging 53 minutes with the fastest service in 49 minutes; first train 00:19, last 23:28.
quote: around 53 minutes... around 77 trains per day... First train departs at 00:19; last train at 23:28... SBB (Swiss Federal Railways) is identified as the main operator of services on this route.

claim: Train tickets from Geneva Airport to Lausanne on SBB start from around €9 (~CHF 9-11).
quote: GENEVA INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT to LAUSANNE train from $11 (€9) with SBB

claim: Lausanne's metro has two lines: the 7.8 km M1 (Flon to Renens, opened 1991) and the 5.9 km M2 (Ouchy-Olympique to Croisettes/Epalinges, opened 2008), the latter a fully automated rubber-tyred driverless metro.
quote: Line M1... 7.8 kilometres (4.8 mi)... Lausanne-Flon... to Renens... Line M2... 5.9 kilometres (3.7 mi)... fully automated, rubber-tyred metro... opened 27 October 2008.

claim: The M2 is the world's steepest metro, with an average gradient of 5.7% and slopes up to 12%, climbing roughly 338 m of elevation between Ouchy on the lake and Croisettes uphill.
quote: the world's steepest metro... an average incline of 5.7%, and as steep as 12% in some places... rubber-tyred metro was selected to counter these, the steepest slopes of any similar adhesion-worked system in the world.

claim: M1 and M2 metro lines run frequently, typically every 5-10 minutes (M2 every 3-5 minutes at peak), making transit the practical way to cover Lausanne's altitude changes.
quote: Both metro lines run frequently, typically every 5-10 minutes... For more specific M2 frequency data, frequency is typically every 3 to 5 minutes, and every 3 to 6 minutes on Sunday.

claim: Lausanne is not an easy walking city because of its three-hill terrain and steep gradients (especially the Old Town); the practical strategy is to combine walking with the M2 metro and funiculars to handle the inclines.
quote: Lausanne is generally not considered an 'easy' city to walk around due to its famously hilly terrain and steep gradients, especially in the Old Town... combine walking with public transport, using the metro or a bus to conquer the steepest inclines.

claim: Lausanne in May averages around 17°C daytime and 9°C at night, with ~126 mm of rainfall and ~212 hours of sunshine.
quote: Lausanne May temperature around 17°C (63°F), with daytime temperatures usually reaching up to 17°C and nighttime temperatures falling to approximately 9°C... averaging around 126 mm for the month... about 212 hours of sunshine.

claim: Lausanne in June averages 21°C daytime and 13°C at night with around 120 mm of rain and 238 sunshine hours — pack layers, a light jacket for evenings, and waterproof gear.
quote: Lausanne June temperature around 21°C (70°F)... cooling down at night to around 13°C... averaging around 120 mm for the month... around 238 hours of sunshine.

claim: Best base areas: Flon/centre for nightlife, dining and metro access; Ouchy for a relaxed lakeside promenade feel; Vieille-Ville/La Cité for medieval streets around the cathedral but with a daily uphill workout.
quote: Flon is a dynamic neighbourhood blending historical charm and modern flair, with vibrant nightlife... Ouchy sits directly on the waterfront and has a much more relaxed feel... La Cité district, where the Cathedral of Notre Dame... if you choose to stay in this area, be prepared for a daily workout as you climb the hill!

claim: Two to three days (a weekend) is the recommended length of stay for Lausanne — enough for museums, Old Town, lakeside and dining without feeling rushed.
quote: With a weekend (two to three days) in Lausanne, you'll have a bit more time to enjoy everything that the city has to offer... Three days is more than enough time to see pretty much everything in Lausanne.
